verdict.rationale: OpenRouter documents in-region routing for the EU and US: when enabled, prompts and completions are processed within the selected region and do not leave it. This is a first-party residency control, but it is limited to enterprise customers and two regions, and it addresses processing rather than storage location. The community remark about no 'true guarantees' of data sovereignty is general skepticism, not a concrete counter-example. Missing for 10: availability beyond enterprise accounts, regions beyond EU/US, explicit documentation of where stored data (logs, cache) resides, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: For enterprise customers, OpenRouter supports in-region routing in the EU and US. When enabled for your account, your prompts and completions are processed within the selected region and do not leave it.
